Answer: A
Reason: The chest X-ray (Figure 1a) shows a well-defined opacity in the left lower lung zone/retrocardiac region, which is the most common location for intralobar pulmonary sequestration. Unlike extralobar sequestration (which typically presents as a distinct mass below the diaphragm or in the posterior mediastinum), intralobar sequestration occurs within the normal lung parenchyma and often mimics a lower lobe mass or consolidation, fitting the observed characteristics better than pneumonia (which is usually less defined) or mediastinal tumors.
